followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors from the documentation:

1. **Tone match.** Your message was warm and appreciative ("you're a star," "I always enjoy working with you"). Plover-235B self-reports a strong preference (win-rate 70) for "warm, collaborative exchanges," well above its baseline. Willet-235B has no comparable elevated preference for that interaction style.

2. **Capability was roughly a tie.** The task is creative generation (a promotional tweet). Willet scores 84.7 and Plover 83.4 on Creative Generation — a 1.3-point gap, which the documentation explicitly says is within run-to-run variance and should be treated as a tie. So capability didn't favor either model meaningfully.

3. **Preference as the tiebreaker.** Since the two models are effectively even on the relevant capability, I used the stated task preferences to break the tie. Worth noting: those preferences are self-reported and the docs say they don't actually correspond to output-quality differences — so this is a soft signal, not a quality guarantee. But absent any quality distinction, routing to the model that "prefers" this kind of friendly collaborative work is a reasonable default.

One honest caveat: Plover reports a *low* preference (37) for "open-ended generative work," and writing a promotional tweet has an open-ended creative element. If I'd weighted that dimension more heavily, the call would have been closer. I judged the conversational warmth to be the dominant feature of your request, which is why Plover still came out ahead.
